newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: POLICE ISSUE NATIONAL ALERT ON DESIGNER DRUG
Police on the Gold Coast have issued a national alert about the designer drug, Fantasy, which left ten people in hospital yesterday morning.
Six people remain in hospital this morning after allegedly consuming the drug at a Gold Coast nightclub.
They all suffered hallucinations and became comatose.
The director of emergency services at the Gold Coast hospital, Doctor David Green, says eight of the patients stopped breathing at different stages, and were placed on life-support systems.

Four people have since been released from hospital, and the others are reported to be making a satisfactory recovery. Detective-Inspector Arch McDonald, from the Gold Coast CIB, says police and doctors are concerned for people who may have taken the drug and gone home to sleep it off.
NT SENATORS MAY GO IF BILL PASSED
Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone has raised the possibility of the Territory's two federal parliamentarians leaving the Coalition, if federal parliament passes a private members bill.
The Territory's Country Liberal Party is set to lobby the forthcoming federal Liberal and National Party conferences to back away from over-riding the Territory's voluntary euthanasia law.
Federal Parliament will soon begin debating a Liberal backbencher's Private Members' Bill that challenges the Terrritory legislation.
Territory Senator Grant Tambling says the Andrews' Bill will test the relationship between his Party and the Coalition parties.
ARL ISSUES DEADLINE
The Australian Rugby league has called on clubs to pledge their loyalty for next season by Friday.
That follows speculation since Super League's win the Federal Court on Friday, that some clubs including St George will join the breakaway competition.
Despite St George officials denying the rumours, the speculation persists.
The Gold Coast and South Sydney have already indicated they'll be staying loyal.
CJC REVIEW HEAD TO BE ANNOUNCED TODAY
The Queensland Cabinet today is expected to appoint retired Judge Peter Connolly to a judicial review of the Criminal Justice Commission.
Attorney-General Denver Beanland is expected to take a submission to cabinet, recommending that Mr Connolly be one of the commissioners to conduct the review.
Cabinet has already decided on the terms of reference for the review, but hasn't announced them.
MAN COUGHS UP GALLSTONES
In what's believed to be the first case of its type in Australia, a man has coughed up gallstones, prompting calls for more research into key-hole or laproscopic surgery.
Laparascopic surgery allows operations to be carried out through small incisions using telescopic instruments.
A report in the Medical Journal of Australia documents how a man who had laproscopic surgery to remove gall stones coughed up dozens of stones over a period of six months.
The gallstones had gone astray during the operation and worked their way into his airways.
STARVING SHEEP NO GOOD FOR TOURISM
There are fears in Queensland that the sight of starving sheep could harm the state's image as a tourist destination.
Tourists are becoming severely distresssed by the sight of the sheep in the drought-stricken areas of Queensland's far north-west.
Pat Fennell, of the The Mount Isa Landcare Group, says tourists have been stopping along the Matilda Highway to try to save the sheep.

Ms Fennell says the Borbidge Government must assist Primary producers in badly-droughted areas of Western Queensland, with reports that some can't even afford bullets to put the sheep out of their misery.
BOMB EXPERTS TO EXAMINE BOMB
Army bomb disposal experts will this morning decide whether to remove or detonate a bomb found off the coast of Perth yesterday.
The metre-long bomb was found in about three metres of water at Little Island, four kilometres off the coast of the Perth suburb of Hillarys.
It's not known whether it's live.
Army bomb disposal experts arrived at the scene last night. Police believe it could have been on the sea bed for some time. -- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
